title: Shafarevich-Tate groups of holomorphic Lagrangian fibrations II

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The proposition assumes '0 ∈ U', where U parametrizes Kähler Shafarevich–Tate deformations. If 0∈U, then X is already Kähler by definition, so the conclusion 'X is hyperkähler' is tautological. The proof and the application to Theorem A(1) require instead that 0 is a limit point of U (0 ∈ \overline{U}), since non-Kähler twists are approximated by Kähler twists.

The theorem states 'Then the following are equivalent:' but no numbered list of conditions appears before the proof. The proof then refers to '(1) ⇒ (2)', '(2) ⇒ (3)', and '(3) ⇒ (1)', so the statement is missing the actual equivalent conditions.

It states: 'The first case occurs if and only if there is a class h ∈ H^2(X) whose restriction to a smooth fiber is non-trivial.' This should be H^2(X^φ). Since X is hyperkähler, such a class on X always exists, which would force b2(X^φ)=b2(X) always, contradicting the second case of the proposition and Theorem C.

It defines H^{0,k}(X^φ):=H^k(X^φ,O_{X^φ}), but then claims the even groups are generated by σ^{k/2}. The form σ is a holomorphic (2,0)-form, so σ^{k/2} lies in H^{k,0}=H^0(Ω^k), not in H^k(O)=H^{0,k}. The generator of H^k(O) should be \bar{σ}^{k/2}. The integral used to prove non-exactness is also malformed, involving σ^nσ^n instead of the appropriate top form involving \bar{σ}.

The proof says 'The cohomology group H^{0,2}(X) is generated by σ' and later 'σ^i ∈ F^i H^{0,2i}(X)'. But H^{0,2}(X)=H^2(X,O_X) is generated by \bar{σ}, not by the holomorphic symplectic form σ, which is of type (2,0). This invalidates the argument as written.

It cites 'Theorem B(2)' for the period map being a local biholomorphism: 'The period map is a biholomorphism in a neighborhood of Y_0 in M_Λ (Theorem B(2)).' However Theorem B of the paper concerns H^1(X^φ,Q)=0 and H^0(Ω^2)=Cσ. The intended reference is Theorem 4.3.4(2), the Local Torelli Theorem.

Several works are cited in the text but absent from the reference list: [SV24] in Remark 1.2.1, [SY22] in the proofs of Theorem 3.0.1 and Proposition 5.3.9, [Voi92] in Theorem 2.1.6, and [Rei70] in Proposition 4.7.1.

The text says: 'Finally, we use a version of [Per17, Theorem 1.15] in Lemma 4.6.1 to conclude...' But Lemma 4.6.1 is about bimeromorphy of two central fibers, not the Kählerness criterion. The cited Perego criterion is actually used in Corollary 4.8.2/Proposition 4.8.3.
